indicators.note: laid out reads as something spread; here out tells us the letters of the three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook spreads a colourful array of spices across the kitchen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal: the letters of SPICE, COOK and LAID are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope shows shifting many-hued patterns, so the adjective describes something vivid with many colours.

clue.text: A doctor stood up for him

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a qualification for a doctor
stood up is to have risen, i.e. rose

explanation.surface: A doctor rose to speak up for a patient who needed support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' defines the answer as a man's name; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrose is a male first name, so a man could be referred to this way.

clue.text: Jacob's brother comes from Eastern U.S.A.

indicators.note: the letters come from a rearrangement of the abbreviation, so the clue signals they are mixed up

parts.note: the abbreviation for the United States, letters used as written

explanation.surface: Someone's sibling Jacob has a brother who hails from the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes from' signals rearranging the letters of U.S.A. after E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau is the elder twin of Jacob, who tricked him out of his birthright.

clue.text: Had a vision which put me in great fear

indicators.note: put me in tells us the word me is placed inside the word for great fear

parts.note: dread is great fear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saw a vision that filled them with terror.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream is to see images in sleep, and a vision is such an experience.

explanation.surface: Making a pot of oats go further for a hungry family.
explanation.walkthrough: PORRIDGE is British slang for time in prison, and so is STRETCH; to stretch food is also to make it last.
explanation.definitionFit: To make supplies last longer is to extend them; a prison sentence is called a term inside in British slang.
Former or erstwhile is one sense; a single occasion is the other.

clue.text: Concentrated on treating tennis elbow initially

indicators.note: treating suggests working on something, so the letters of tennis are worked into a new order
initially picks just the first letter of elbow

explanation.surface: A physio focused on curing a player's tennis elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' rearranges TENNIS to INTENS; 'initially' gives E from elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intense is strong and undiluted, as a powerful flavour is.

parts.note: killing time usually means idling, but read literally it is the period when hunters may shoot game

explanation.surface: Someone passing idle hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of the year when game may legally be shot is a season for killing.

explanation.surface: Wondering whether travellers around the world come from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harlem Globetrotters are a famous American exhibition basketball team.
explanation.definitionFit: People who tour the world widely are travellers of the globe; the Harlem basketball team carries the same name.

explanation.surface: A slight hint of a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin umbra, shadow, and also means offence taken or resentment.

indicators.note: about here means moved around, telling us the letters of article are reordered

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reviewing a musical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but signals rearranging ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo musical performance, often by one pianist or singer, is a kind of concert.

explanation.surface: A soldier seized and fired upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Seized a prisoner is one sense; photographed, as in snapped a picture, is the other.

indicators.note: develop means change and grow, so the letters of it may are reworked into another word

explanation.surface: An acquaintance could perhaps grow into a closer bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful goodwill between people or nations is friendly relations.

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone arrived just to embarrass you.
explanation.walkthrough: A snub nose is short and turned up; to snub someone is to rebuff them pointedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and upturned describes a certain nose; to slight someone publicly is to humiliate them.

clue.text: Raise the roof about student coming bottom

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed roof wraps round the student
in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner, the plate a student driver displays

explanation.surface: A student causes a racket, then ends up last in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns ROOF upward to FOOR; 'about' puts it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground surface of a room is its lowest part.

explanation.surface: Taking precedence over a senior figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier in time is one sense; the head of a religious house, ranked under an abbot, is the other.

parts.note: need is want or poverty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being poor made someone annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or annoyed by repeated jibes.

clue.text: Farmers may combine to gather it in

definitions.text: Farmers may combine to gather it in

parts.words: Farmers may combine to gather it in
parts.note: combine looks like a verb of joining forces, but a combine is the big machine that reaps and threshes the crop

explanation.surface: Farmers band together to bring in the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop gathered at season's end is what is collected from the fields.

parts.note: people proverbially drown their troubles in alcohol, not water

explanation.surface: Something that seldom drowns in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Griefs and troubles are what people drown in drink, so these are woes.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words in court are one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A commotion breaking out during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in court' looks like a location, but it is the fodder rearranged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy quarrel or uproar.

clue.text: Peak calls turned out to be about Further Education

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reordered letters go round the abbreviation
turned out means rearranged, so the letters of calls are reordered

parts.note: FE is the British abbreviation for Further Education, study after school

explanation.surface: Calls to a mountain turn out to concern further education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges the letters of calls; 'about' wraps them round FE. Scafell is a mountain in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Scafell is a summit in the Lake District, so it is a mountain top.

clue.text: Head off disaster and have a party with fruit

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed from the word for disaster

parts.note: havoc is widespread destruction or disaster
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Avert catastrophe by throwing a celebration with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent' but removes H from HAVOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Eric's an unusual type of poisoner

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of Eric's an are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Eric is a strange sort of murderer using poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ERIC'S AN; the possessive s counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a classic toxic element, a kind of poison used to kill.

clue.text: Apply for directions to one's house

explanation.surface: Requesting instructions for finding someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: To address oneself to a task is to apply oneself; the street details of a home are the other sense.

explanation.surface: A crafty way to prop something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means sly or mischievous; a curved structure holds up weight in buildings and bridges.

parts.note: vital statistics are bust, middle and hip measurements, and the middle one sits in the centre

explanation.surface: A central office for important figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the three measurements of a figure, the middle one is the body's narrowest midsection.

clue.text: Entrance, by using commercial with sex-appeal

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Making an entrance by using an attractive advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film 'It' starring Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine, its way in.

clue.text: I am repeatedly uplifted by an operatic role

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means the letters read from bottom to top
repeatedly tells us the contraction for I am is written twice

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone feels lifted again and again by a part in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles IM to IMIM; 'uplifted' turns it to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the seamstress heroine of Puccini's La Boheme, a famous soprano part.

clue.text: Boat produced by company somewhere in Cornwall?

indicators.note: in tells us the company abbreviation is placed inside the letters for the region

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West, SW, of England; the question mark marks the definition by example

explanation.surface: A vessel built by a firm based in a Cornish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county at England's south-western tip, so the region abbreviation SW stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying freight.

clue.text: Love cereal, if put inside the mouth

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: put inside tells us the word if goes within the word for a cereal

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loves putting cereal in their mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening in the body, and the mouth is such an opening.

indicators.note: can be broken suggests the letters of rule can are smashed and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A core regulation may be violated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like part of 'can be broken', but it belongs to the fodder RULE CAN; 'be broken' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear relates to a nucleus, the core of something.

parts.note: reads as returning to the past, but describes motion opposite to the way a clock's hands go

explanation.surface: Travelling into the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning against the direction of a clock's hands runs counter to its movement.
